extracted.intended_audience: general public and policymakers interested in US foreign policy and postwar reconstruction
extracted.subtask_short: news reporting on US foreign policy
extracted.subtask_description: Contemporary newspaper reporting covering U.S. foreign-policy decisions, Congress actions, and international relief/reconstruction programs (Marshall Plan, trusteeship agreements, reparations policy) in mid-1947. Includes summaries of committee recommendations, presidential messages, and related procedural notes for Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trusteeship agreement conformity with US policy and UN Charter
rubrics_metrics.description: Its terms are in conformity with the policy of this Government and with its obligations under the Charter of the United Nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President's message to Congress notes the trusteeship agreement (approved by the Security Council April 2, 1947) was proposed by the U.S. and accepted with changes; the statement frames conformity with U.S. policy and UN Charter obligations as a necessary condition for seeking congressional action to bring the agreement into force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trusteeship agreement must promote inhabitants' development while protecting US security
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms of the agreement make economic, social and educational development of the inhabitants of the trust territory, and at the same time fully protect the security interests of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President emphasizes a dual standard for the Pacific islands trusteeship: (1) substantive commitments to economic, social and educational development for inhabitants, and (2) adequate safeguards for U.S. security interests; he argues these combined aims justify prompt congressional approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method for international agreement (constitutional permissibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Either method (joint resolution or treaty) is constitutionally permissible and the agreement will be of the same effect internationally and under the supremacy clause whether advised and consented to by the Senate or whether approval is authorized by a joint resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President explains he considered both submission methods and, while both are legally permissible, he recommends congressional action by joint resolution in this specific instance because of the 'interest of both Houses'—this provides procedural guidance about how to present such agreements to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make aid 'productive' by ending reparations and reducing punitive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: If we are to make this help productive, we should have to insist on putting an end to current reparations and on cutting down the earlier punitive programs of reparations aimed at weakening Germany and Japan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: House Foreign Affairs subcommittee's two-point program for Europe's recovery asserts productive U.S. aid depends on ceasing reparations and reversing punitive policies toward former Axis powers; this is presented as a policy criterion for structuring postwar assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set industrial levels enabling self-support and export surplus
rubrics_metrics.description: Set new levels of industry that would enable Germany and Japan to balance their own needs for imports and create export surplus which we could direct into the rebuilding of the rest of Europe and the necessary reconstruction of the Far East.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcommittee recommendation: industrial policy for Germany and Japan should be calibrated to restore domestic sufficiency and produce exportable surplus to finance broader regional reconstruction; presented as an economic/design criterion for recovery programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aid programs must be 'sound business' for the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: One question, it said, must be answered in formulating an overall aid program: ... must be sound business for the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subcommittee frames U.S. assistance not only in humanitarian/political terms but as requiring economic justification—aid proposals should be evaluated on whether they represent prudent, beneficial investments for the U.S. (a fiscal/strategic criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broaden participation: more complete cooperation yields greater resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic theory of officials was that the more complete the cooperation the greater the resources; willingness to let other nations take part (even if Soviet participation is limited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diplomatic reasoning reported around Marshall-plan discussions: maximizing participating nations increases pooled resources and effectiveness; practical guidance for designing multilateral recovery schemes is to include as many cooperating partners as feasible.
